researchSummary.finding: Operator is live and active. The company is legally registered as BLACK MOUNTAINS CYCLE CENTRE LTD (Companies House 09053176, incorporated 22 May 2014, status Active) but has rebranded publicly to 'Dirt Farm Wales', operating at dirtfarm.wales. Phone, email, address, GPS, opening hours, services, and a TripAdvisor rating were all verified from official/operator sources. Google Business Profile rating was not findable — this task blocker remains unresolved. Cover image and logo remain blocked (no CC-licensed or permission-cleared assets found). An editorial decision is required on display name before this entry can be published.

description.short: Dirt Farm (Black Mountains Cycle Centre) is a purpose-built downhill and freeride mountain bike park set on a working hill farm in the Black Mountains, five miles north of Abergavenny. Featuring Blue, Red, Black, and Pro-grade trails designed by Shaun Bevan and Gary Broad, the park offers uplift sessions Wednesday to Sunday with push-and-ride access most days.
description.shortNote: Drafted from verified website and tourism source content. Uses both names to aid search discoverability pending editorial name decision. Do not add commercial claims.
description.full:
Dirt Farm, legally trading as Black Mountains Cycle Centre Ltd, is a specialist downhill and freeride mountain bike park located at Great Llwygy Farm on the eastern edge of the Black Mountains, approximately five miles north of Abergavenny, Monmouthshire.

The facility was established in 2014 and the trails were designed by experienced riders and trail builders Shaun Bevan and Gary Broad. The park features a range of trails across four grades: Blue (intermediate), Red (experienced intermediate), Black (advanced/expert), and a Pro jump line for professional-level riders. Trail features include a dramatic bridge, large table-tops, flowing berms, and modular sections that allow riders to mix and match lines.

Uplift sessions run Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Bank Holiday Mondays from 10am to 6pm (first uplift 10am, last uplift 4pm). Thursday evening uplift sessions run from 4pm to 8pm. Push-and-ride access is available on most open days. Winter opening hours vary; riders should check the online booking calendar. The venue is closed Mondays and Tuesdays except Bank Holiday Mondays.

Facilities on site include limited parking (car sharing encouraged), a portaloo, a bike wash area, snacks and hot drinks, and weekend food service by 'Farmer Mark Eats'. Gateway Cycles operates a pop-up repair and spares service. Bike hire is not available at the site; Drover Cycles in Hay-on-Wye offers rentals nearby. A holiday cottage on the farm is available via Airbnb.

All riders must complete an online waiver prior to arrival and comply with the park's Riders Code of Conduct. Riders under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

claimsNeedingHumanReview.claim: National Park boundary: 'heart of the Brecon Beacons' marketing claim
claimsNeedingHumanReview.detail: Multiple third-party sources repeat the operator's own marketing language: 'set in the heart of the Brecon Beacons National Park'. The postal address (Abergavenny, Monmouthshire, NP7 7PE) and nearest settlement (Pandy) are close to but may be outside the Brecon Beacons NP boundary. A human editor should verify using NRW or OS boundary data before repeating this claim. If the site is not within the NP boundary, use 'near the Brecon Beacons' instead.

The VisitWales listing shows blackmountainscyclecentre@gmail.com which is likely a pre-rebrand contact. The current operator email (hello@dirtfarm.wales) is confirmed from the live website. The operator should be encouraged to update their VisitWales listing, but this does not block the directory entry.
